newsitem.title: USA: Viacom Q4 results helped by MTV, Paramount.
newsitem.headline: Viacom Q4 results helped by MTV, Paramount.

text.p: Viacom Inc said on Tuesday its fourth quarter results were helped by growth at its MTV Networks and Paramount units.

Networks and broadcasting revenues increased 23 percent to $703 million while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) for the sector increased 40 percent to $253 million, it said.

MTV Networks revenues increased 30 percent to $399 million and EBITDA rose 45 percent to $176 million, mainly due to higher ad and affiliate revenues. Ad revenue gains were driven by continued ratings growth at Nickelodeon, it said.
The company said its Showtime Networks Inc unit's revenues and EBITDA increased 13 percent and eight percent, respectively.
Television station revenues and EBITDA increased 14 percent and 38 percent, respectively.

The entertainment segment benefited in the fourth quarter from the strong performance of Paramount Pictures unit's feature films and first run syndication television programming, which resulted in a 34 percent increase in revenues to $1.1 billion and a 97 percent increase in EBITDA to $81 million, Viacom said.

Increased revenues reflect the strong foreign and domestic performance of "Mission: Impossible," and domestic theatrical release of "Star Trek: First Contact," "The First Wives Club" and "Beavis and Butt-Head Do America," the company said.
It said The quarter also benefited from higher domestic syndication revenues for television programming, principally "Star Trek: Deep Space Nine."

Video and Music/Theme Parks fourth-quarter revenues rose 18 percent to $1.0 billion, reflecting an increase in the number of company owned video stores as well a six percent rise in worldwide same-store sales, the company said.

For the quarter, it said its Simon & Schuster publishing unit posted a 12 percent increase in revenues to $641 million driven by strong sales from Higher Education, Educational Technology, International, and Macmillan Publishing USA.
The Higher Education division's performance was primarily attributable to a strong front list and the successful integration of Internet and CD-ROM technology into textbooks.
The Educational Technology Group, including Computer Curriculum Corporation and Educational Management Group, benefited from school districts' increased use of electronic instruction, Viacom said.
It said International and Macmillan Publishing USA benefited from strong title sales and an enhanced focus in the Asian and Latin American markets.
